[[File:Logo Naruto Shippūden.svg|alt=The Naruto: Shippuden logo, where there is a yellow to orange gradient in each letter while the subtext is blue.|250px|frameless|right]]
''[[Naruto: Shippuden]]'' is an [[anime]] television series mainly adapted from [[List of Naruto chapters (Part II)|Part II]] of [[Masashi Kishimoto]]'s original ''[[Naruto]]'' [[manga]] series, with exactly 500 episodes. It is set two and a half years after the [[Naruto (TV series)|original series]] in the ''Naruto'' universe, following the teenage ninja [[Naruto Uzumaki]] and his allies. The series is directed by [[Hayato Date]], and produced by [[Pierrot (company)|Pierrot]] and [[TV Tokyo]]. It began broadcasting on February 15, 2007, on TV Tokyo, and concluded on March 23, 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://mediaarts-db.jp/an/anime_series/9886|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161001190711/http://mediaarts-db.jp/an/anime_series/9886 |archive-date=October 1, 2016 |script-title=ja:NARUTO疾風伝 |language=ja |website=Media Arts Database |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2017-03-23/naruto-shippuden-anime-ending-on-500th-episode-confirmed/.113787 |title=Naruto Shippūden Anime's Ending on 500th Episode Confirmed |publisher=[[Anime News Network]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170323123510/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2017-03-23/naruto-shippuden-anime-ending-on-500th-episode-confirmed/.113787 |archive-date=March 23, 2017 }}</ref>

On January 2, 2009, [[Viz Media]] and [[Crunchyroll]] provided eight English [[Subtitle (captioning)|subtitled]] ''Naruto: Shippuden'' episodes on the official ''Naruto'' website.<ref name="Campaign2"/> Later the following 2 weeks, Viz began providing subtitled versions of the latest ''Naruto: Shippuden'' episodes a week after they first aired in Japan, with a new episode being added to the ''Naruto'' website each subsequent Thursday.<ref name="Campaign2">{{cite web|url=http://www.viz.com/news/newsroom/?id=169|title=A New Generation, A New Destiny|date=November 17, 2008|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216075136/http://www.viz.com/news/newsroom/?id=169|archive-date=December 16, 2008}}</ref> On July 24, 2009, Viz Media announced that the series would be released on the [[iTunes Store]].<ref name="English Dubbed Naruto Shippuden Episodes 1-8 on iTunes">{{cite web|url=http://www.viz.com/news/newsroom/?id=343|title=Viz Media Brings the latest Naruto: Shippuden Story Arc to iTunes For Digital Download|publisher=[[Viz Media]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090805030031/http://www.viz.com/news/newsroom/?id=343|archive-date=August 5, 2009}}</ref> The first DVD release of the series in North America was released on September 29, 2009.<ref name="Region1 dvds announced">{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B001RIZ8WE|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307185526/http://www.amazon.com/dp/B001RIZ8WE|archive-date=March 7, 2016|title=Naruto Shippuden, Vol. 1|website=Amazon}}</ref> The English [[dubbing|dub]] of ''Naruto: Shippuden'' made its US premiere on [[Disney XD]] on October 28, 2009.<ref name="Naruto Shippuden Dub">{{cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-23/viz-confirms-plans-to-present-new-dubbed-naruto|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114142722/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-23/viz-confirms-plans-to-present-new-dubbed-naruto|archive-date=November 14, 2016|title=Viz Confirms Plans to Present New Dubbed Naruto|publisher=[[Anime News Network]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-27/naruto-shippuden-main-english-dubbing-cast-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114081346/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-27/naruto-shippuden-main-english-dubbing-cast-announced|archive-date=November ''Naruto: Shippuden'' stopped airing on Disney XD on November 5, 2011, after 98 episodes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.toonzone.net/schedule/displaySeries.php?seriesID=327&networkID=17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319194657/http://www.toonzone.net/schedule/displaySeries.php?seriesID=327&networkID=17|archive-date=March 19, 2012|title=Naruto Shippuden Disney XD schedule|date=December 11, 2009|publisher=toonzone.com|url-status=dead}}</ref> The English dub was streamed on the [[Neon Alley]] [[Streaming television|web channel]] from its launch in October 2012, and beginning December 29 of the same year with episode 99, dubbed episodes premiered every week until March 25, 2016, after 338 episodes, about a month before Neon Alley's closure. [[Adult Swim]]'s [[Toonami]] programming block began airing the anime from the beginning on January 5, 2014, restarting from Episode 1, in an uncut format.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2014-01-03/naruto-shippuden-debuts-on-adult-swim-toonami-this-sunday-at-12-30am|title=Naruto Shippuden Debuts on Adult Swim's Toonami This Sunday 1/5 at 12:30AM|date=January 3, 2014|work=[[Anime News Network]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140208030816/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2014-01-03/naruto-shippuden-debuts-on-adult-swim-toonami-this-sunday-at-12-30am|archive-date=February 8, 2014|url-status=live|df=mdy-all}}</ref> The network started showing never before aired dubbed episodes at the 339th episode mark by May 2021 to September 2024.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://comicbook.com/anime/news/naruto-shippuden-dub-new-episodes-toonami-milestone/|title=Naruto Shippuden Hits New Toonami Milestone|date=May 2, 2021|work=[[ComicBook.com]]|author=Nick Valdez|access-date=January 2, 2023|archive-date=January 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230102173318/https://comicbook.com/anime/news/naruto-shippuden-dub-new-episodes-toonami-milestone/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In Japan, ''Naruto Shippuden'' aired continuously year-round with regular preemptions for specials and sporting events taking place, not being split into standard seasonal cycles.}}

== Home media release ==
In four regions, episodes from the series have been released on DVD and Blu-ray by single volumes and box sets. In Japan, twenty-six sets of volumes have been released based on which arc it represents. In North America, twelve single volumes and thirty-eight box sets have been released. In the United Kingdom, thirty-eight box sets and ten series sets have been released. In Australia and New Zealand, thirty-eight collections, five box sets, and a different collection of seven have been released.
